p: Bless the LORD: He wakens his dulness to praise God, showing that both understanding and affections, mind and heart, are too little to set forth his praise.
forgiveth all thine iniquities: That is, the beginning and chiefest of all benefits, remission of sin.
destruction: For before we have remission of our sins, we are as dead men in the grave.

youth is renewed like the eagle's: As the eagle, when her beak overgrows, sucks blood and so is renewed in strength, even so God miraculously gives strength to his Church above all man's expectations.
Moses: As to his chief minister, and next to his people.
chide: He shows first his severe judgment, but as soon as the sinner is humbled, he receives him to mercy.
dealt with us after our sins: Who have proved by continual experience that his mercy has always prevailed against our offences.
the east is from the west: As great as the world is, so full is it of signs of God's mercies toward his faithful when he has removed their sins.
man: He declares that man has nothing in himself to move God to mercy, but only the confession of his infirmity and misery.
righteousness unto children's children: His just and faithful keeping of his promise.
covenant: To whom he gives grace to fear him, and to obey his word.
his angels: In that we, who naturally are slow to praise God, exhort the angels, who willingly do it, we stir up ourselves to consider our duty and wake from our sluggishness.
